data.title: Tesla adds Model Y V2L in Canada, then quietly removes it less than 24 hours later
data.description:
Tesla has once again created confusion over Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) availability in Canada. Less than 24 hours after adding the feature to the Model Y Premium AWD and Performance on its Canadian website, the company has quietly removed it from both variants.

As we reported yesterday, Tesla had updated its Canadian Model Y lineup with new features, including V2L capability for the Premium All-Wheel Drive (AWD) variant.

However, looking at Tesla’s website on Friday afternoon revealed that the feature had disappeared entirely, not just from the Premium AWD, but also from the Model Y Performance.

Screenshots captured Thursday evening by Drive Tesla clearly showed both variants supporting “Vehicle to load (120V 20A AC) with charge port and Outlet Adapter.” That would have allowed owners to draw up to 2.4 kW of power from the vehicle’s battery through an Outlet Adapter connected to the charging port.

By Friday afternoon, that wording has been removed.

The sudden reversal raises questions about whether Tesla accidentally published the feature, essentially a copy and paste error from launches elsewhere in the world, and whether the Canadian Model Y was ever V2L compatible in the first place.

At this point, Tesla has not provided an explanation for the change.

The situation is particularly confusing given that Tesla has already introduced V2L on the Model Y in other markets, including in the U.S. and China over the past week.

The unannounced change is even more frustrating because this is not the first time an apparent error like this has happened. Earlier this year there was confusion surrounding V2L availability this year on the Model Y Performance, as well as numerous specification errors on the Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD) when it was announced.

All of this makes an official clarification important for Canadian buyers who may have placed an order based on the specifications displayed before they were removed.

For now, Tesla’s Canadian website no longer lists V2L capability on any Model Y variant. Whether that changes again remains to be seen, but we will update this story if Tesla provides more information.

data.title: Nearly Half of Canadians Want an EV, but Price and Selection Remain Barriers
data.description:
Key Points
  • 48% of Canadians now lean toward an EV, up from 45% in April
  • Interest is highest among 18- to 29-year-olds, at 67%
  • 42% of EV-inclined buyers may wait for more Chinese models, and 37% for more electric pickups
  • 69% want public chargers to take debit or credit cards without an app

Nearly half of Canadians are leaning toward an electric vehicle for their next purchase, but a new poll shows why some interested shoppers might still hold off.

Abacus Data’s latest survey for Clean Energy Canada puts EV interest at 48%, compared with 45% in April and in 2025. Released October 9, the results also show that vehicle selection matters to people already considering the switch.

Among those leaning toward electric, 42% said they might wait until more Chinese EVs are available. Another 37% identified a lack of electric pickup choices as a concern about buying this year. These responses describe possible reasons to wait, rather than firm decisions to postpone a purchase.

Price is another part of the picture. Although upfront cost remains the biggest barrier, many potential buyers have limited knowledge of less expensive vehicles already on the market.

In this group, which excludes Canadians certain to choose either gas or electric, 60% were at least somewhat aware of new EVs costing $30,000 to $40,000. Only 20% were very aware. Awareness was lower for used models priced from $20,000 to $30,000, at 52% overall and 14% very aware.

That contrasts with broader knowledge of EV ownership costs. Within the same group, 69% knew electric vehicles are cheaper to own and drive, while 62% knew about the $5,000 federal rebate for eligible new vehicles.

The survey also asked what Canadians want from their vehicle market. European influence attracted 47% support, versus 21% for U.S. influence, after respondents considered the effect on brands, models, sizes and EV choices.

For public charging, the preference was clearer – 69% supported requiring chargers to accept debit or credit payments without an app, rising to 75% among EV-inclined Canadians.

Abacus surveyed 2,762 adults online from September 18 to 23 and weighted responses to reflect Canada’s population.

data.title: Tesla Supercharger under construction in Deschambault [Quebec]
data.description:
Tesla is adding another charging stop along Quebec’s Highway 40, with a new Supercharger now under construction at Restaurant Le Chavigny in Deschambault.

The location only appeared on Tesla’s Find Us map earlier this week, and now construction is already underway. Le Chavigny announced the start of construction in a Facebook post, confirming it was working with Tesla to bring several fast-charging stalls to the property.

According to the restaurant, the current schedule calls for installation and activation before the end of 2026. While the number of stalls was not confirmed in the post, the image shared in it indicates it could be up to 16 stalls. Although we’re not quite sure how accurate that is because the cars are parked in the bushes, and it shows older V3 hardware.

Located at 11 Rue des Pins, just off Exit 254, Le Chavigny sits between Trois-Rivières and Quebec City. Its highway access and on-site restaurant should make it a convenient place to plug in while stopping for a meal during a longer drive through the Portneuf region.

Deschambault joins other recent Supercharger projects in Quebec. Tesla is also building a station in Montcerf-Lytton, while a station in Brownsburg also started construction this week.

Tesla also recently opened a 24-stall location in Mont-Tremblant on September 29, featuring a commemorative stall marking the company’s 3,000th Canadian Supercharger.

data.title: Tesla AI Renamed Tesla Super Intelligence on X
data.description:
Tesla has made a small but notable change to its presence on X, renaming its Tesla AI account to Tesla Super Intelligence, just days after Elon Musk confirmed plans to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI.

The account, previously known as TeslaAI (@TeslaAI), now uses the handle @TeslaSI and displays “Tesla Super Intelligence” as its name. 

The update follows Musk’s comments on October 4, when he confirmed that SpaceXAI would be renamed SpaceXSI, replacing “AI” with “SI,” short for “Super Intelligence.”

At the time, Musk replied to a user asking about the proposed change, saying, “Yes, we will make that change.” He later added in a separate post, “No more AI.”

As for why Tesla beat SpaceXAI to the punch? That may simply come down to the complexity of changing a company name compared to updating an X account. A corporate name change can involve legal filings and other administrative steps, while changing an account’s display name and handle is relatively straightforward. 

Why the change from AI to SI?

The new terminology follows an executive order signed by U.S. President Donald Trump on September 29, directing federal agencies to use “Super Intelligence” instead of “Artificial Intelligence” in official communications where permitted by law.

SpaceXAI itself only received its current name in July, following SpaceX’s acquisition of xAI in February. The company introduced the SpaceXAI branding and a new logo just three months ago.

For now, Tesla’s account appears to be the first to adopt the new Super Intelligence naming convention, while the more significant SpaceXAI rebrand remains pending.

data.title: Tesla Urges Owners to Charge to 100% Ahead of Hurricane Isaias, Prepares Mobile Superchargers
data.description:
Tesla is urging owners along the U.S. Gulf Coast to prepare for Hurricane Isaias by fully charging their vehicles, while the company gets ready to respond to potential disruptions across its Supercharger network.

In an update shared Thursday, Tesla recommended that owners with access to home charging charge their vehicles to 100% before the storm arrives. The extra range could prove valuable if widespread power outages make charging difficult or residents need to evacuate.

Tesla also pointed owners to the car’s screen and the Tesla app for live Supercharger availability.

The warning comes as Hurricane Isaias approaches the northern Gulf Coast. According to the National Hurricane Center’s Friday morning update, the storm had strengthened into a major hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph (195 km/h) and was expected to make landfall Friday night or early Saturday.

Forecasters are warning of dangerous storm surge, heavy rainfall, flooding, and potentially damaging winds across portions of Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.

Tesla Ready to Deploy Mobile Superchargers

Beyond encouraging owners to prepare, Tesla is also taking steps to keep its charging infrastructure operational.

Before the hurricane arrives, the company’s priority is maintaining Supercharger uptime. Once the storm passes, attention will shift to restoring affected stations and deploying temporary charging infrastructure where needed.

That could include Tesla’s Megapack-powered mobile Superchargers, which can provide charging without relying directly on the local electrical grid.

Tesla has used these mobile charging setups for years, including during busy holiday travel periods. When owners first spotted one in November 2019, at the Madonna Inn Supercharger in San Luis Obispo, California, it paired a Megapack with eight Urban Supercharger stalls, and drivers reported peak rates of up to 125 kW. Tesla hasn’t said what current units deliver.

Tesla outlined a similar strategy ahead of Hurricane Milton in October 2024.

data.title: Tesla China posts best month of 2026, extending growth streak
data.description:
Tesla China finished September with its strongest monthly wholesale sales of 2026, extending its growth streak as Giga Shanghai continues supplying customers at home and overseas.

According to China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) figures released on Friday, Tesla recorded 95,366 Shanghai-built Model 3 and Model Y sales last month. That was up 5% from 90,812 a year earlier, marking the eleventh consecutive month of year-over-year growth.

The total is a wholesale figure and includes vehicles destined for China and elsewhere, including Canada, Europe, Australia and other Asia-Pacific markets. 

September also improved on August’s 86,166 vehicles by 10.7%, beating July’s previous yearly high of 93,579. Through the first nine months, Tesla China’s wholesale volume reached 743,060 vehicles, an increase of 22.54% compared with the same period in 2025.

Tesla China Monthly Wholesale Sales

Includes domestic deliveries and exports. Source: CPCA | Chart: Drive Tesla

As we reported last month, Shanghai exports had already more than doubled through August, helping offset weaker deliveries within China. That shift has made the factory increasingly important to Tesla’s international supply, with exports representing just over half its wholesale volume through August.

September continued that trend. Exports rose 58.3% year-over-year to 30,529 vehicles, while domestic deliveries declined 9.4% to 64,837. For the full third quarter, Shanghai wholesale sales reached a record 275,111 vehicles, up 13.7% from last year.

Tesla China January–September Wholesale Sales

Includes domestic deliveries and exports. Source: CPCA | Chart: Drive Tesla

Part of Giga Shanghai’s success is thanks to Canada, as Tesla now sources Canada’s Model 3 lineup from Shanghai. Recently, delivery estimates for the Model 3 were stretching into December 2026 and January 2027, but after the upgrades announced last night, some variants no longer even have an estimated delivery date.

data.title: Rivian Goes All-In on Ghostbusters With Halloween Software Update
data.description:
Rivian is bringing a little Hollywood magic to its vehicles this Halloween, teaming up with Sony Pictures for a Ghostbusters-themed software update that turns its electric trucks and SUVs into ghost-hunting machines.

The limited-time Halloween Mode begins rolling out today, October 9 and will be available through November 2, 2026, bringing new animations, lighting effects, sounds, games, and hidden surprises to Rivian vehicles.

At the centre of the update is a dedicated Ghostbusters app, featuring a retro-inspired interface and a large red switch that activates the experience from the in-car display. Owners can choose from several themed light and sound effects, including the Ecto-1 siren, Proton Pack, Slimer, and Ghost Trap.

There’s also a new Trick or Treat Mode that plays the iconic Ghostbusters theme song while coordinating the vehicle’s displays, interior lighting, and exterior effects. Some features can even be activated remotely through the Rivian mobile app, allowing owners to surprise unsuspecting trick-or-treaters.

For those who enjoy hunting for Easter eggs, Rivian has hidden Ghostbusters characters throughout its infotainment system. There’s also a new ‘Mallow Mash arcade game where players race to catch Mini-Puft marshmallow characters while parked.

Rivian Builds Its Own Ghostbusters Ecto-1

Rivian isn’t stopping at software. Rivian has also turned R1S SUVs into Ecto-R1s, six of them according to MotorTrend, inspired by the original Ghostbusters Cadillac. They feature the familiar red graphics, Ghostbusters logos, and roof-mounted equipment, including sirens, spotlights, and a radar dish.

The vehicles will appear at Rivian retail locations and Halloween events, while original Ghostbusters star Bill Murray is helping promote the collaboration in a new commercial.

Somebody called? ☎️👻 Dr. Peter Venkman and the Ecto-R1 are on the case. This year, Ghostbusters takes over Rivian’s Halloween mode, with our latest software update starting tomorrow. Learn more at https://t.co/PUYBG2TYUX https://t.co/rOldfRunAb

— Rivian (@Rivian) October 8, 2026

The update continues Rivian’s tradition of elaborate Halloween features, following previous themes inspired by Back to the Future and Knight Rider. Tesla has already rolled out its own Halloween Mode in software update 2026.38.3, but Rivian’s latest offering takes the seasonal fun to another level.

Owners will need software version 2026.36.0 for R1 vehicles or 2026.36.40 for the R2, along with the latest Rivian mobile app.

data.title: Tesla renames FSD ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe
data.description:
Tesla has started calling Full Self-Driving (Supervised) ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe, with the new name now on its UK, German and Dutch websites, days after Germany said Tesla had offered the rebrand during talks over EU-wide approval.

Tesla’s website describes a system that can steer, change lanes, navigate to a destination and park, all while the driver supervises. The page also stresses that the system doesn’t make the car autonomous.

Tesla offered the name in September talks with Germany’s Transport Ministry, which had called ‘FSD’ somewhat misleading for a system that still needs an attentive driver. The ministry now backs EU-wide approval, and the name wasn’t the only thing the two sides settled.

Germany and Tesla also settled on a 10% ceiling for how far the system may drive above the limit, and Germany says it will back that cap in the EU approval process. Speed Offset can currently set the car’s speed as much as 50% over the detected limit, and Tesla hasn’t said whether its European build already enforces the lower cap.

The company has already published a video demonstrating the re-named feature.

$TSLA [테슬라 TAD – Tesla Assisted Driving] 테슬라는 유럽에서 명칭을 변경한 TAD(구 FSD)가 적용된 새로운 비디오를 공개하였음 차량 내 관련한 모든 문구가 Assisted Driving 으로 표시되는 것을 볼 수 있음 https://t.co/IGykZRG7UF

— Tsla Chan (@Tslachan) October 9, 2026

The changes come at an important time for Tesla. The company has already secured national approvals in eight European countries, including the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark and Czechia, but has faced opposition from Sweden and France over speeding concerns.

The EU-wide vote has already slipped from October and won’t come before December.

With Germany now supporting Tesla’s efforts, and the new name already appearing on its websites, the company has addressed one of the concerns surrounding FSD’s European rollout. Whether those changes will be enough to secure broader approval remains to be seen.

data.title: Tesla Canada Ordered to Pay $162,000 After Model X Catches Fire in Montreal
data.description:
Tesla Canada has been ordered to reimburse insurer Intact $161,700 over a 2020 Model X that caught fire in Montreal, according to the Superior Court decision.

During the proceedings, a Tesla employee suggested that vehicle fires were generally associated with misuse or deliberate damage. Justice Ian Demers rejected Tesla’s application to overturn the default judgment Intact had secured in June, finding that the company had failed to provide supporting evidence or raise a sufficiently credible defence.

Sacha De Santis was behind the wheel of his Model X in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, with his partner beside him, around 1 a.m. on March 5, 2023, as reported by TVA Nouvelles.

Shortly after they switched on the heat, the couple noticed a smell of smoke coming from inside the vehicle. They stopped, took their things and left the car. Within approximately five minutes, the Model X was engulfed in flames and ultimately declared a total loss.

“It could have gone really badly. We were lucky,” De Santis told TVA Nouvelles (translated from French).

Insurer Takes Tesla to Court

A 2023 police investigation found no sign of a crime. Intact Assurance paid out $161,700 for the write-off, then went after Tesla Canada for the money.

The insurer argued that the Model X was still covered by Tesla’s basic vehicle warranty, which provides coverage for four years or 80,000 kilometres.

An expert report presented to Quebec Superior Court indicated the fire originated near the passenger-side dashboard, with a premature electrical failure considered the probable cause.

The ruling turned down Tesla’s bid to overturn a default judgment; it wasn’t a full trial on what caused the fire.

Tesla Canada has not publicly commented on the ruling, and the period for filing an appeal had not yet expired at the time of publication.

data.title: Geely officially confirms Canadian launch, first vehicles coming in 2027
data.description:
Just one week after launching its Canadian website, Geely has officially confirmed its plans to enter the Canadian market, with the Chinese automaker saying its first vehicles will arrive in 2027.

The announcement follows the launch of geely.ca earlier this month, which initially offered few details beyond confirming the company’s intentions to establish a Canadian dealer network. Now, Geely has provided a timeline and additional details about its expansion.

According to Geely Auto Group, the company has already started establishing local operations and developing a retail and service network across Canada. The automaker says it is working with experienced local partners to support customers both during and after their vehicle purchases.

“Canada represents an important next step in Geely Auto’s international growth,” said Bryan Wu, Managing Director of Geely Auto Canada. “We are entering this market with a long-term commitment, bringing our global technology and engineering capabilities to Canadian drivers while building strong local partnerships and the support customers need to feel confident in choosing Geely. We know that trust is earned over time, and we are committed to earning it here.”

Geely has not yet revealed which vehicles it plans to sell in Canada, nor has it announced pricing or dealership locations. Those details are expected to be shared as the company gets closer to its commercial launch next year.

The company has been preparing for its Canadian entry for several months. In April, Geely began recruiting senior executives in Toronto, followed by sightings of EX5 and EX2 test vehicles arriving at Toronto Pearson in May.

Geely is one of several Chinese automakers preparing to enter Canada following Ottawa’s decision to allow up to 49,000 Chinese-built EVs annually at a reduced 6.1% tariff. BYD and Chery’s Omoda and Jaecoo brands have also launched Canadian websites, although none have started selling passenger vehicles here under their new brands.
